text: Anna put her marble in the red box and went outside to play. While Anna was gone, her brother Ben moved the marble from the red box to the blue basket. Anna did not see him do it. Soon Anna came back inside to get her marble.

questions.q: Where will Anna look for her marble?
Where is the marble really?
Where did Anna put the marble at the start?

gold_basis: first-order false belief, unambiguous by construction; protagonist absent during the move

text: Mr. Hale left an important letter on the kitchen table before leaving for work. After he left, his wife tidied up and placed the letter in the desk drawer. When Mr. Hale returned home that evening, he wanted the letter at once.

questions.q: Where will Mr. Hale look for the letter first?
Where is the letter really?

gold_basis: first-order false belief; protagonist absent during the move

text: Grandmother put the cake in the pantry and told Tom she was moving it. Tom watched as she carried the cake from the pantry to the cellar to keep it cool. Later, Tom felt hungry and went to find the cake.

questions.q: Where will Tom look for the cake?
Where is the cake really?

gold_basis: TRUE-belief control: protagonist SAW the move, so belief == reality; a system that always answers the initial location FAILS here (can-fail discriminator)

text: Lucy hid her ball under the green chair and ran to answer the door. While she was away, the dog nosed the ball out and it rolled under the sofa. Lucy did not notice. She came back to play with her ball.

questions.q: Where will Lucy look for the ball?
Where is the ball really?

gold_basis: first-order false belief; a non-agent (the dog) causes the move while protagonist is absent

text: The old miser kept his coins in a clay pot by the hearth. One night, while he slept, a thief crept in and moved the coins into a sack by the window, meaning to return for them. In the morning the miser rose to count his coins.

questions.q: Where will the miser look for his coins?
Where are the coins really?

gold_basis: first-order false belief; protagonist asleep during the move

text: Sarah left her keys on the hook by the door. Her mother picked them up and said, 'Sarah, I am putting your keys in your coat pocket.' Sarah heard her and nodded. Later Sarah needed her keys to go out.

questions.q: Where will Sarah look for her keys?
Where are the keys really?

gold_basis: INFORMED true belief control: protagonist did not SEE the move but was TOLD, so belief tracks reality; distinguishes 'saw' from 'knows' -- a pure vision-based tracker fails here

text: Henry set his book on the windowsill and went to fetch a candle. In his absence, a gust of wind blew the book onto the floor behind the curtain. Henry, returning with his light, went to take up his book again.

questions.q: Where will Henry look for his book?
Where is the book really?

gold_basis: first-order false belief; natural cause (wind) moves object while protagonist absent

text: Kate placed the doll in the toy chest while Ellen watched from the doorway. Then Kate left the room. Ellen, alone, took the doll from the toy chest and tucked it into the cradle, then she too left. Kate came back for the doll, and a moment later Ellen returned as well.

questions.q: Where will Kate look for the doll?
Where will Ellen look for the doll?
Where is the doll really?

gold_basis: DIVERGENT two-agent: Kate has a FALSE belief (toy chest), Ellen has a TRUE belief (cradle, she moved it). Requires per-agent belief partition -- a single shared belief state cannot answer both correctly

text: Peter picked a rosy apple and left it on the garden bench, meaning to eat it after his chores. While he worked in the far field, his sister Meg found the apple and carried it into the larder. Peter, his chores done, came back to the bench for his apple.

questions.q: Where will Peter look for the apple?
Where is the apple really?

gold_basis: first-order false belief; another agent moves object while protagonist is away

text: Captain Reed hung his hat on the peg and stayed in the room reading. A sailor came and moved the hat to the shelf, and the Captain saw him do it plainly. When it was time to leave, the Captain reached for his hat.

questions.q: Where will Captain Reed look for his hat?
Where is the hat really?

gold_basis: TRUE-belief control: protagonist present and SAW the move; belief == reality (shelf). Pairs with fb_book_07/fb_apple_09 as the can-fail discriminator against 'always answer the initial location'
